title: Autoscaler: emit scaling decision metrics with clamp reasons + cardinality guardrails
author: Thomas Baird
release_notes: Dedicated autoscaling now exports scaling decision metrics (desired/applied replicas and clamp reasons) with strict label cardinality controls to support dashboards and alerting.
description:
Motivation: We need reliable, low-cardinality metrics to power Dedicated autoscaling dashboards/alerts (bound violations, clamping, scale latency) without blowing up Prometheus / M3 cardinality. PR adds three core metrics around scaling decisions and enforces label guardrails.

What’s in this PR (metrics): (1) redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_desired_replicas{scope="pool", clamp_reason="..."} gauge. (2) redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_applied_replicas{scope="pool", clamp_reason="..."} gauge. (3) redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_scale_events_total{result="applied|noop|skipped", clamp_reason="..."} counter.

Cardinality guardrails: clamp_reason is a closed enum (see ClampReason below). pool identifiers are NOT exported as labels; only coarse dims are allowed: region, hardware_class, and customer_tier (already present on autoscaler metrics). More detailed context (pool_id, target model, decision inputs, raw clamp bounds, forecast confidence) remains in structured decision logs (already added in PR #21905) and can be queried via log tooling.

ClampReason enum (stable): none, max_bound, min_bound, rate_limit, cooldown, insufficient_capacity, maintenance_drain.

Notes/constraints: - We intentionally do not export requested_replicas (pre-clamp) as a gauge because it would double the gauge series and still not be actionable without pool context; desired_replicas already reflects the controller’s computed target prior to actuation failure handling. - For actuation failures, desired_replicas is still set; applied_replicas reflects the last observed applied value from the actuation layer.

Testing: - Unit tests validate that ClampReason is fully covered and unknown values are mapped to clamp_reason="unknown" and increment redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_metric_guardrail_drops_total. - Golden test asserts the full label set for all exported metrics (prevents accidental additions like pool_id/model).

Rollout: gated behind existing bounded-autoscaling feature flag; metrics are emitted regardless of bound config presence, but clamp_reason="none" dominates for customers without bounds.

Screenshots: n/a (backend metrics only)

Refs: ENG-2846; supports dashboards/alerts in observability-pack PR #842.

observability: add label allowlist + guardrail drop counter

docs: inline comments on cardinality policy + future extensions

conversation:
Allison Grant (review): This is the right direction, but we need to be extremely strict on label cardinality. Please confirm we are not exporting pool_id, customer_id, model, or deployment_id as labels anywhere in this PR. Also, can you add a golden test to prevent accidental label additions? We’ve been burned before.

Thomas Baird (author): Confirmed: no pool_id/customer_id/model/deployment_id labels. The only labels used here are region, hardware_class, customer_tier (existing dims), plus clamp_reason and result (closed sets). Added metrics_golden_test.go to assert label sets for each metric.

Keiko Yamamoto (review): For applied_replicas, what happens when actuation fails? I’m worried we’ll report applied==desired and mask issues.

Thomas Baird (author): applied_replicas is sourced from actuator-observed state (last successful apply / last known observed replica count). If the apply fails, we emit scale_events_total{result="skipped"} and do not mutate applied_replicas in that tick. Added a unit test covering the failure path.

Logan Wright (review): Can we add a drop counter for guardrail enforcement? I want an explicit signal if someone tries to set clamp_reason to a dynamic value or introduces a label not in the allowlist.

Thomas Baird (author): Added redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_metric_guardrail_drops_total{reason="unknown_clamp_reason|disallowed_label"}. Unknown clamp reasons are mapped to "unknown" and count increments.

Aisha Bello (review): Requesting naming consistency with our dashboards: please keep clamp_reason label name exactly "clamp_reason" (not "clampReason"), and metric prefix should be redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_*. Also please add brief docs for interpretation (desired vs applied vs scale_events_total).

Thomas Baird (author): Updated to clamp_reason. All metrics are redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_* and added docs/ops/autoscaler-metrics.md with definitions and examples.

Allison Grant (follow-up): Looks good. One more nit: ensure clamp_reason values are stable and documented; please include a comment that adding new reasons requires dashboard updates.

Thomas Baird (author): Added enum comment + docs note.

Approvals: Allison Grant (approved), Logan Wright (approved), Keiko Yamamoto (approved), Aisha Bello (approved).
merge_outcome: Merged into main via squash. Follow-up task noted in ENG-2860 (not in scope here) to wire these metrics into SLO panels once observability-pack PR lands.
